sections_en.text: This document sets out the calibration steps I1 to be carried out annually, as indicated by the code Y1 above.

The first draft of this document was prepared by Eng. Abdel Monem Ibrahim Heikal and Mrs. Asmaa Abdel Monem, reviewed by Eng. Wagdy Eid Mansour, tested by Eng. Marwa El-Hadidy, endorsed by General Manager Eng. Yousry Ahmed Abdel Maksoud, reviewed by Eng. Abdel Monem El-Emam, Manager of the Instruments and Electricity Department in the Inspection Sector of the East Delta Electricity Production Company, and approved by Eng. Fathy Mahmoud Ragab, Head of the Talkha Power Station Sector.

It was endorsed by Eng. Samir Abdel Galil, General Manager of Inspection and Quality at the East Delta Electricity Production Company and MPIS Coordinator, and approved by Mr. Mahmoud Mohamed Sleiman, General Manager of Financial and Administrative Control and Supervisor of the Inspection and Quality Control Sector.

items: Issue a work order, with an industrial safety category card available for the site workers
Fence off the area and use the appropriate warning signs
Use occupational safety and health equipment such as a safety helmet and safety shoes, etc.
Suitable tool kit, occupational safety and health equipment

sections_en.text: Number of cards to be tested: 10 cards per gas unit; number of units: 8
Number of gates to be tested per card: 9

rows: Switch off the Power switch feeding the MK-II Speedtronic, located inside the Speedtronic.
Remove the external terminal block on the isolate cards.
Withdraw the ten cards and take them to the laboratory.
Feed the card with 125 Vdc (+ 65 on pin 11), (- 65 on pin 10)
Test the first gate as follows:

Make a jumper between the +ve on pin 11 and the Input on pin 1; the expected result is that the lamp of this gate lights, which means this gate is sound. If the lamp does not light, this means one of two things: either the lamp is burnt out and the gate is sound - in this case it is determined that the lamp is burnt out by measuring the voltage ±12 V at the gate output on pin 5, which should be 12 Vdc; if the voltage is 12 Vdc, this means the gate is sound and the lamp is replaced - or the lamp is burnt out and the gate is not sound; this case is recognised by measuring the voltage at the gate output on pin (5): if there is no voltage, this means the gate is not sound, so the gate components are checked, the faulty ones are replaced, and the test is repeated by measuring the voltage at the gate output, finding it 12 Vdc; if the lamp still does not light, it is replaced. This completes the testing of the gate.
Repeat the above steps on the remaining eight gates
Repeat steps 1-6 for each of the ten cards.
Refit the cards in their places.
Reconnect the Power.
Make sure the unit is Ready by placing the start switch in any position (Crank or Fire or Auto); the Ready lamp lights, confirming that all the unit circuits are ready for operation
Make sure there are no alarms on the alarm panel

Introduction
This document sets out the calibration steps I1 to be carried out annually, as indicated by the code Y1 above.
The first draft of this document was prepared by Eng. Abdel Monem Ibrahim Heikal and Mrs. Asmaa Abdel Monem, reviewed by Eng. Wagdy Eid Mansour, tested by Eng. Marwa El-Hadidy, endorsed by General Manager Eng. Yousry Ahmed Abdel Maksoud, reviewed by Eng. Abdel Monem El-Emam, Manager of the Instruments and Electricity Department in the Inspection Sector of the East Delta Electricity Production Company, and approved by Eng. Fathy Mahmoud Ragab, Head of the Talkha Power Station Sector.
It was endorsed by Eng. Samir Abdel Galil, General Manager of Inspection and Quality at the East Delta Electricity Production Company and MPIS Coordinator, and approved by Mr. Mahmoud Mohamed Sleiman, General Manager of Financial and Administrative Control and Supervisor of the Inspection and Quality Control Sector.
Safety precautions
Issue a work order, with an industrial safety category card available for the site workers
Fence off the area and use the appropriate warning signs
Use occupational safety and health equipment such as a safety helmet and safety shoes, etc.
The unit is shut down
Tools and equipment used
Suitable tool kit, occupational safety and health equipment
Digital voltmeter, Fluk 187
Complete tool kit
DC power supply + 65 Vdc
Procedures to be carried out
Number of cards to be tested: 10 cards per gas unit; number of units: 8
Number of gates to be tested per card: 9
Testing the ISOLATE card
Switch off the Power switch feeding the MK-II Speedtronic, located inside the Speedtronic. | 1.
Remove the external terminal block on the isolate cards. | 2.
Withdraw the ten cards and take them to the laboratory. | 3.
Feed the card with 125 Vdc (+ 65 on pin 11), (- 65 on pin 10) | 4.
Test the first gate as follows: | 5.
Make a jumper between the +ve on pin 11 and the Input on pin 1; the expected result is that the lamp of this gate lights, which means this gate is sound. If the lamp does not light, this means one of two things: either the lamp is burnt out and the gate is sound - in this case it is determined that the lamp is burnt out by measuring the voltage ±12 V at the gate output on pin 5, which should be 12 Vdc; if the voltage is 12 Vdc, this means the gate is sound and the lamp is replaced - or the lamp is burnt out and the gate is not sound; this case is recognised by measuring the voltage at the gate output on pin (5): if there is no voltage, this means the gate is not sound, so the gate components are checked, the faulty ones are replaced, and the test is repeated by measuring the voltage at the gate output, finding it 12 Vdc; if the lamp still does not light, it is replaced. This completes the testing of the gate. | 6.
Repeat the above steps on the remaining eight gates | 7.
Repeat steps 1-6 for each of the ten cards. | 8.
Refit the cards in their places. | 9.
Reconnect the Power. | 10.
Make sure the unit is Ready by placing the start switch in any position (Crank or Fire or Auto); the Ready lamp lights, confirming that all the unit circuits are ready for operation | 11.
Make sure there are no alarms on the alarm panel | 12.
